idiom_name: Jinja2 template with {% %} statements (also Mako for full Python in the template)
implementation_notes: Python's standard library covers only interpolation (str.format, string.Template, f-strings), so the script-in-the-view step up comes from a library: Jinja2 provides {% %} statements, {{ }} expressions, loop and conditional blocks and autoescaping, with |safe and Markup as the deliberate opt-outs, while Mako permits arbitrary Python in the template and Django's template language is the deliberately restricted end of the same range. The classic structure remains justified where a page is a one-off; otherwise keep the fetch in the handler and the template to presentation, which also makes the view testable with a plain dict.
pitfalls: Autoescaping is a property of the environment and the file extension: a template loaded with an unexpected suffix, or an Environment built without autoescape, renders raw values silently.
|safe, Markup and {% autoescape false %} are the injection switches; wrapping user text in Markup is Python's phrasing of Razor's Raw and needs the same justification.
Fetching inside a template hides I/O where it is hard to test and instrument: queries in the template make transaction boundaries and caching unpredictable.

Undefined variables are not errors by default (they render empty or fail only on attribute access), so a misspelled field produces a blank page instead of a failure unless StrictUndefined is configured.
